findings.risk: Why dangerous: Without CSP, the browser has no policy restricting script sources. Injected XSS payloads execute freely, enabling session theft and defacement.
Why dangerous: Without X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors), the page can be iframed by attackers, enabling clickjacking to trick users into actions.
Why dangerous: Without HSTS, users can be downgraded to HTTP via SSL-stripping MITM attacks, exposing cookies and credentials in plaintext.
Why dangerous: Without nosniff, browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute user-uploaded content as scripts.
Why dangerous: Without a Referrer-Policy, full URLs (with tokens/params) leak to third-party sites via the Referer header.
Why dangerous: Without Permissions-Policy, embedded content may access sensitive browser features (camera, geolocation, mic) on your pages.
Why dangerous: Legacy header, largely deprecated; modern browsers ignore it. CSP is the correct modern control.
